ledger.summary: By the shortest road they reach Higham a little before sunset; the gate is barricaded with men-at-arms and bowmen. A knight of the town refuses entry to men bearing the Dry Tree, calling them strong-thieves. Ralph's brother Hugh, a poorly armed man-at-arms sworn to Higham, slips through the barrier and joins him. The knight threatens to sally; Ralph offers to meet them man for man. The hundred Dry Tree riders arrive over the hill and the knight retreats behind the barrier, shooting a bolt and some arrows harmlessly. Ralph will not fight; they skirt the walls out of bowshot and ride by moonlight for the down country, Hugh riding beside Ralph.
ledger.geography_notes: Higham-on-the-Way is reached before sunset from the Scaur by the shortest road. Strong barriers stand before the gate. The company skirts the town walls out of bowshot and heads for the down country by moonlight.
